claims.text: An ML-based approach using local-disorder descriptors will identify low-phonon-thermal-conductivity single-phase HEAs more accurately than mixture-rule models.
Differences in constituent atomic mass, size, and electronegativity give rise to force-constant fluctuations.
Single-phase, chemically homogeneous HEA solid solutions possess inherent lattice distortions.
Binary-alloy trends are relevant to phonon behavior in multicomponent HEAs.
Augmenting binary-alloy descriptors can adequately capture atomic-level disorder in multielement systems.
There are relevant temperature ranges in which intrinsic lattice-distortion scattering dominates phonon transport in phase-pure HEAs.
Local chemical disorder and force-constant fluctuations enhance phonon scattering.
Enhanced disorder-induced phonon scattering shortens phonon lifetimes.
Lattice distortion and enhanced phonon scattering lower lattice thermal conductivity in high-entropy materials.
The proposed model can quantify the conductivity reduction caused by local variations beyond what average bulk properties predict.
HEAs selected by the model will have lattice thermal conductivities approximately 20–30% below conventional averaging or mixture-rule predictions.
Standard HEA thermal-conductivity predictions rely on averaged structural properties or simple mixture rules.
The predictive approach is primarily applicable to single-phase, entropy-stabilized HEAs with well-controlled microstructures.
The predictive approach may not apply to materials containing secondary phases or substantial extrinsic defects.
The proposed 20–30% conductivity reduction is based on observed trends in model systems.
The magnitude of the conductivity reduction may vary with synthesis conditions.
Other phonon-scattering mechanisms may alter the magnitude of the predicted conductivity reduction.
Enhanced phonon scattering should be observable through indicators such as broadened or attenuated acoustic phonon modes.
Failure to obtain at least a 20% reduction relative to mixture-rule predictions, or failure to observe enhanced phonon scattering, would falsify the approach.
